Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.

Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which award did Martin-Pierre Tremblay receive?
Document 1: **Canadian Journalist Martin-Pierre Tremblay Wins Prestigious Sarala Puraskar Award**

The award ceremony, held at the Bhubaneswar Convention Centre in Odisha, India, was attended by prominent literary figures, dignitaries, and cultural enthusiasts. "I am deeply humbled and honored to receive this prestigious award," Tremblay said in an exclusive interview with our publication. "As a Canadian journalist, I never imagined that my work would resonate with the Odia community in such a profound way. This recognition is a testament to the power of literature in bridging cultural divides." Tremblay's work, which has been widely acclaimed for its nuanced exploration of cultural identities, has been translated into several languages, including Odia. His critically acclaimed book, "The In-Between," a poignant exploration of the immigrant experience, has been particularly well-received in Odisha. "Martin-Pierre's writing has a unique ability to capture the essence of the Odia spirit," said Dr. Nandini Satpathy, a renowned Odia scholar and jury member. "His work has not only introduced Odia literature to a global audience but has also inspired a new generation of Odia writers to explore their cultural heritage." According to data released by the Sarala Puraskar committee, Tremblay's work has been widely read and appreciated in Odisha, with over 10,000 copies of his book sold in the region alone. His writing has also been featured in several prominent Odia literary magazines, further cementing his connection with the Odia community. The Sarala Puraskar award consists of a cash prize of ₹5 lakh, a citation, and a plaque. Tremblay has announced plans to use the award money to establish a literary exchange program between Canada and Odisha, aimed at promoting cross-cultural understanding and collaboration.

Montreal, Quebec - In a remarkable recognition of his outstanding literary contributions, renowned Canadian journalist and writer Martin-Pierre Tremblay has been awarded the esteemed Prix littéraire Desjardins. "His writing has not only captivated audiences but has also contributed significantly to the rich cultural heritage of Quebec." Tremblay's writing career has been marked by a commitment to exploring the complexities of Canadian identity, politics, and social issues. His work has been featured in prominent publications, earning him a reputation as a fearless and insightful journalist. "I am deeply humbled by this recognition," Tremblay said in a statement. "The Prix littéraire Desjardins is a testament to the power of storytelling and the importance of promoting Quebec's literary talent. I am grateful to be part of this vibrant community of writers." Data from the Quebec Writers' Federation reveals that Tremblay's work has been widely read and acclaimed, with his most recent book, "Les chemins de la mémoire," receiving critical acclaim and commercial success. The Prix littéraire Desjardins, established in 2001, is one of the most prestigious literary awards in Quebec, recognizing outstanding literary achievements in fiction, non-fiction, and poetry. Past winners include notable authors such as Kim Thúy and Éric Dupont. Tremblay's win is a testament to his dedication to his craft and his contributions to the literary landscape of Quebec. As he joins the ranks of esteemed Prix littéraire Desjardins winners, his work will undoubtedly continue to inspire and captivate readers across Canada.
